texts: Final pages. Every computation the universe will ever perform, converging on a single point at the end of time: the $(item)Omega Point$(). It is the last thing you can make.

Frank Tipler's 1994 idea: a collapsing universe in which computation speeds up without limit, so infinite thought fits before the end. Cosmology has since argued against it. Mine exists anyway - and a Zero-Point Extractor will happily run on it for ten hours.
Bostrom asked whether we live in a simulation. The $(item)Reality Compiler$() takes it literally: if the universe is a simulation, this decompiles it.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 6$() machine.
This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts.

The final machine. Decompile reality into $(item)Source Code Fragments$(), forge $(item)Reality Anchors$(), and finally compile the $(item)Omega Point$() - which a Zero-Point Extractor can burn for 10 hours.$(br2)If I am wrong about the simulation, the error messages will be very interesting.
